subject: Urban Planning
title: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure
description: Learn Climate-Resilient Infrastructure in one minute.

hook.text: Houston designed its bayous for a 100-year storm. Harvey was a 1,000-year storm. The infrastructure was overwhelmed.

buildup.text: Climate change makes extreme weather more frequent. Infrastructure designed for yesterday's climate fails under today's storms.

discovery.text: The Netherlands builds infrastructure for a 10,000-year flood. Their levees, barriers, and water systems are world-leading.

twist.text: Building for extreme events is expensive. But rebuilding after each disaster costs far more — and the costs keep rising.

climax.text: Resilient infrastructure means redundancy, flexibility, and designing for the worst case — not just the expected case.

punchline.text: Design for the 100-year storm. Get hit by the 1,000-year storm. Nature doesn't read plans.

quiz.question: Why does traditional infrastructure design fail under climate change?
options: Construction materials degrade faster in warmer temperatures
Systems designed for historical weather patterns can't handle new extremes
Climate change causes earthquakes that damage underground pipes
